title: Microsoft 365 Backup: Full Workload Backup policies for SharePoint, OneDrive and Exchange
summary: Hold: the briefing reports automation and spending-control details as undocumented when Microsoft publishes them, including OneDrive and Exchange exclusion APIs and the fact that budgets do not stop billing. It also needs corrections to workload-specific permissions, coverage exceptions and notification setup. The roadmap dates, rollout notice and published storage price are accurately reported.

claims.claim: Full Workload Backup allows an administrator to protect SharePoint, OneDrive or Exchange with a single policy for that workload.
claims.quote: a new capability that allows admins to quickly protect an entire workload (SharePoint, OneDrive, or Exchange) with a single policy.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; What's changing; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Every eligible item outside custom policies and the exclusion list is protected by Full Workload Backup.
claims.quote: Full Workload Backup automatically protects all eligible protection units that aren't already included in a custom backup policy, added to the exclusion list, or in the process of being permanently deleted from Microsoft 365 Backup.
claims.fix: Qualify the coverage statements with the additional documented exception: 'Full Workload Backup protects eligible items that are not in a custom policy, on the exclusion list, or in the process of being permanently deleted from Microsoft 365 Backup.'

claims.claim: The policy-creation documentation says Exchange recipient types such as room and group mailboxes are unsupported.
claims.quote: Other Exchange recipient types, such as room and group mailboxes, are not supported at this time.

claims.claim: Eligibility remains undefined for Full Workload Backup, including whether room or group mailboxes and legacy SharePoint templates qualify.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Backup supports both user mailboxes and shared mailboxes. Other Exchange recipient types, including room mailboxes and group mailboxes, aren't supported.
claims.fix: Do not reopen product-wide exclusions as unknown for this policy. Replace the Scope sentence with 'Microsoft 365 Backup supports user and shared mailboxes, but not room or group mailboxes, and excludes some SharePoint templates.' Remove the eligible-items open question, or narrow it to 'Are there additional eligibility restrictions specific to Full Workload Backup beyond Microsoft 365 Backup's documented supported mailbox and site types?' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/backup/backup-faq.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no Graph or PowerShell call for creating a Full Workload Backup policy.
claims.quote: New-MgBetaSolutionBackupRestoreSharePointProtectionPolicy ... [-DisplayName <string>] ... [-ProtectionMode <string>] ... Create a protection policy for a M365 service SharePoint. Policy will be created in inactive state.
claims.fix: Replace the blanket absence with 'The Microsoft.Graph.Beta.BackupRestore module documents New-MgBetaSolutionBackupRestoreSharePointProtectionPolicy with a -ProtectionMode parameter; the Graph resource defines fullServiceBackup as the entire-workload mode. The REST create reference does not list that property.' For controls[0].api, use powershell call "New-MgBetaSolutionBackupRestoreSharePointProtectionPolicy -DisplayName '<policy-name>' -ProtectionMode fullServiceBackup" and the cited cmdlet URL; qualify the note that this creates an inactive SharePoint policy, not an activated policy, and that the REST create reference is inconsistent with the beta PowerShell surface.

claims.claim: The Exchange-specific creation walkthrough does not list a back-up-all option.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Backup full workload backup create protectionMode fullServiceBackup Graph PowerShell OneDrive Exchange exclusion units. Read backup-view-edit-policies: its Exchange walkthrough lists CSV, dynamic rules and filters, but no back-up-all option.

claims.claim: The dedicated Full Workload Backup creation steps do not mention a Recovery window.
claims.quote: On the Review and finish page, review the configuration, and then select Next to create the Full SharePoint Backup policy.
claims.fix: Remove this open question: the dedicated subsection indeed omits the setting, but the same page places Back up all SharePoint sites and Back up all OneDrive accounts before Backup Settings, where a Recovery window is set. Its general recovery-window section applies the window to every artifact in a policy; subsection silence is misleading evidence of an undocumented retention rule.

claims.claim: The policy-creation walkthrough includes setting a Recovery window.
claims.quote: Select Next to move to the Backup Settings page, where you can provide a name for your policy and set the Recovery window.

claims.claim: Whether Microsoft 365 Backup policy and item limits apply to Full Workload Backup, and what to do above them, remains an open question.
claims.quote: These limits apply to each workload independently (SharePoint, Exchange, and OneDrive). ... up to 100 backup policies per workload. ... up to 100,000 items per backup policy. ... contact Microsoft to discuss options for a higher scale.
claims.fix: Replace the open question with 'Microsoft publishes limits of 1,000,000 items per workload, 100 backup policies per workload and 100,000 items per backup policy, and directs organisations needing higher scale to contact Microsoft.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/backup/backup-overview#backup-scale-limits. Do not imply that Full Workload Backup is exempt from the published product-wide limits.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, email notifications
claims.claim: Turning on Microsoft 365 Backup email notifications is sufficient for a second administrator to see policy changes.
claims.quote: By default, recipients are notified only about potentially harmful events, but you can also opt in to receive notifications for routine events. ... Add users ... to the Backup Notification List. ... Select the checkbox to also receive routine event notifications.
claims.fix: Replace the checklist bullet with 'Turn on Microsoft 365 Backup email notifications, add the second administrator to the Backup Notification List, and select the checkbox to receive routine events, including policy creation and modification. Jobs configured with a 10-minute RPO are excluded; notification events trigger when the overall policy completes.'

claims.claim: A medium risk rating is justified by coverage and spend growth after an administrator enables this optional control.
claims.quote: risk: "medium"; defaultState: "admin-opt-in"; 'nothing is protected by it until an administrator creates the policy.' The standard defines low risk to include 'nothing happens until an admin opts in.'
claims.fix: Set risk to low and use the rationale 'Low. Nothing is protected by Full Workload Backup until an administrator enables it; existing custom policies remain unchanged.' Keep the post-enablement coverage and spend cautions in the body.

claims.claim: The exclusion CSV upload on the Exclude sites step is optional.
